summary: ARES-NAV is a decision-support concept for Mars Extravehicular Activity (EVA) navigation and science planning. To solve scattered mission data, difficult terrain, and strict resource limits, it integrates five core data layers—optical imagery, topography, thermal context, geology, and rover observations—into one aligned map view. Through a structured workflow, crews can assess hazards and review routes while keeping human judgment in control. It is important because it connects terrain safety with science goals at sites like Jezero Crater to enable safer, more focused planetary exploration
details:
• What it does / How it works: ARES-NAV is a decision-support concept for Mars Extravehicular Activity (EVA) navigation and science planning. It integrates five core data layers (optical imagery, topography, thermal context, geology/minerals, and rover observations) into one aligned map viewthrough a 4-step workflow: Select, Compare, Assess, and Review.
  • Benefits & Impact: Overcomes scattered mission data, difficult terrain, and strict resource limitsto enable safer route reviews and focused planetary exploration at sites like Jezero Crater, while keeping human judgment firmly in control.
  • Tech Stack: Built with React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS on the frontend, powered by a Node.js backend.
  • Creativity & Factors Considered: Instead of relying on an automated "black box" risk score, safety is treated as a comprehensive review process evaluating terrain mobility, crew resources, environmental factors, and data uncertainty.
